name: The Italian Game
description: The classic, open, aggressive opening for White. Ideal for mastering piece development, controlling the center, and attacking the weak f7 square.

chapters.title: Two Knights & The Fried Liver Attack
chapters.subtitle: Punishing 3... Nf6 with 4. Ng5! d5 5. exd5

steps.title: Claim the Center
steps.explanation: We stake an immediate claim on d5, free our Light-squared Bishop, and open the diagonal for our Queen.
steps.warning: Never start with passive pawn moves like a3 or h3 — always claim the center first!

steps.title: Black Equalizes the Center
steps.explanation: Black mirrors our move, staking their claim on d4.

steps.title: Develop With a Threat
steps.explanation: We develop our Knight toward the center while immediately attacking Black's unprotected e5 pawn.

steps.title: Black Defends e5
steps.explanation: Black develops their Knight to protect the e5 pawn.

steps.title: The Italian Bishop
steps.explanation: The signature move! Our Bishop locks eyes on f7 — the weakest square in Black's camp, guarded only by their King.

steps.title: Two Knights Defense
steps.explanation: Black counter-attacks our e4 pawn instead of playing 3... Bc5.

steps.title: Double Attack on f7
steps.explanation: We strike! Both our Bishop on c4 and Knight on g5 target the f7 pawn. Black has only ONE good defense: 4... d5.
steps.warning: 4... h6? is an instant blunder! White plays 5. Nxf7 winning the Queen or Rook.

steps.title: Black Blocks the Bishop
steps.explanation: Black blocks the bishop's sightline to f7 with their center pawn.

steps.title: Open the Center
steps.explanation: We capture on d5 with our pawn, continuing the relentless assault.
steps.warning: If Black plays 5... Nxd5?, we play 6. Nxf7! Kxf7 7. Qf3+ Ke6 8. Nc3 (The true Fried Liver Sacrifice) dragging their King into mate!

steps.title: The Main Line Counter
steps.explanation: Black avoids the Fried Liver trap and attacks our bishop.

steps.title: Check with Tempo!
steps.explanation: We don't retreat our bishop passively — we deliver a check on b5, forcing Black to block with 6... c6.

chapters.title: Giuoco Piano (The Quiet Game)
chapters.subtitle: Handling 3... Bc5 with 4. c3 & 5. d4 center dominance

steps.title: Pawn to e4
steps.explanation: Open the game by claiming the central d5 and f5 squares.

steps.title: Black Responds
steps.explanation: Black mirrors in the center.

steps.title: Attack e5
steps.explanation: Develop with tempo by directly threatening Black's e5 pawn.

steps.title: Defense
steps.explanation: Black guards the pawn.

steps.title: Target f7
steps.explanation: Place the Bishop on its best diagonal aiming at f7.

steps.title: The Giuoco Piano
steps.explanation: Black develops symmetrically, challenging our dominance.

steps.title: Prepare d4
steps.explanation: The master plan! We play c3 to support a massive pawn push to d4 next move, taking full control of the board.

steps.title: Black Attacks e4
steps.explanation: Black targets our e4 pawn.

steps.title: Strike in the Center!
steps.explanation: We push d4! Our pawns dominate the center, attack Black's bishop on c5, and seize total control.

chapters.title: Defending as Black (Two Knights Counter)
chapters.subtitle: How Black refutes 4. Ng5 with 4... d5 & 5... Na5!

steps.title: White Opens
steps.explanation: White claims the center with 1. e4.

steps.title: Mirror the Center
steps.explanation: We stake our equal claim on d4 and free our pieces.

steps.title: White Attacks e5
steps.explanation: White attacks our pawn.

steps.title: Defend with Knight
steps.explanation: We guard our e5 pawn and develop toward the center.

steps.title: The Italian Bishop
steps.explanation: White points at our f7 square.

steps.title: Two Knights Counterattack!
steps.explanation: We counter-attack White's e4 pawn! We dare White to attack f7.

steps.title: White Tries to Attack f7
steps.explanation: White piles up on our f7 pawn.

steps.title: Block the Bishop!
steps.explanation: The ONLY correct move. We sacrifice a pawn to shut down White's bishop diagonal.
steps.warning: Never play 4... h6? or 4... Bc5? here — White wins immediately on f7!

steps.title: White Takes on d5
steps.explanation: White takes our pawn.

steps.title: Counterattack White's Bishop!
steps.explanation: The Grandmaster move! We DO NOT recapture with 5... Nxd5? (which walks into the Fried Liver). Instead, we attack White's bishop on c4, winning initiative!
steps.warning: DO NOT play 5... Nxd5? — 6. Nxf7! crushes Black!
